pr_body:
This PR essentially fixes #4858, but it does so by revamping the `DropOnTimeline` command after I realized that it is actually not practical to store the dropped layers in a vector of pointers to layers because of how the `ObjectId`s impact on the logic needed to keep them in sync. So I used the same approach as in other commands: use a `stringstream` object to store the data (dropped layers) that needs the redo operation.

As a side effect, I believe that there is a high chance that the following crashes are fixed as well:
[ASEPRITE-2QF](https://igara-studio.sentry.io/issues/6085369687/events/ff0e50ded22d4bcbc4330aa777f531b9/)
[ASEPRITE-2QB](https://igara-studio.sentry.io/issues/6084029246/events/c3edf8fd1b1449a010abf680ebd561c5/)
pr_comments:
A couple of points before I review this:
1) Probably we could use some smart pointers for the Doc* (check #4852)
2) Although we are using `std::stringstream` to serialize `doc::Object`s, in a future I'd like to avoid doing so, and serialize objects only when it's necessary (e.g. to save undo info to disk/.aseprite format, https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/issues/3718#issuecomment-1453512657 ), but I have that on mind from a long time but never created the issue (it's a refactor for the future), I'll create a new issue about that now

> 1. Probably we could use some smart pointers for the Doc* (check [Use some smart pointers (unique_ptr) in 
DropOnTimeline::onExecute() / getNextDocFromImage() #4852](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/issues/4852))

Sure, no problem.

> 2. Although we are using `std::stringstream` to serialize `doc::Object`s, in a future I'd like to avoid doing so, and serialize objects only when it's necessary (e.g. to save undo info to disk/.aseprite format, [Saved Undo History #3718 (comment)](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/issues/3718#issuecomment-1453512657) ), but I have that on mind from a long time but never created the issue (it's a refactor for the future), I'll create a new issue about that now

I've just saw it...avoiding it for the DropOnTimeline command was a real pain just because I couldn't keep the ObjectIds on objects in memory because of the checks that are done to avoid objects with the same id. My idea was to keep a copy of the dropped layers in memory as a vector of Layer* objects, then when a redo operation took place, I just used that vector to generate the layers again, and that was the root of the problems, because when creating the copies I needed to keep the original ids of the objects, so then I tried to save the ids in a separate vector...but when I realized that I should keep all the ids of groups, image layers, cels, and what not...the code got smelly...
So, how do you think we should deal with this situation? 
Anyway, at least the DropOnTimeline command just serializes once on command execution and deserializes each time a redo is done, there is no serialization/deserialization on undo.

> So, how do you think we should deal with this situation?

At the moment probably the best is to keep the layers serialized, and then investigate #4860 to avoid the serialization on all `Cmd`s (anyway we'll need some way to keep the serialization available to save it in the undo history inside .aseprite files in the future).

issue_context.title: Crash when undoing the drop of a layer after being deleted
issue_context.body:
Sentry Issue: [ASEPRITE-2QT](https://igara-studio.sentry.io/issues/6094992079/?referrer=github_integration)

```
EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION_READ / 0xb6: Fatal Error: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION_READ / 0xb6
  File "xutility", line 5987, in std::_Find_unchecked
    const auto _Result    = _STD _Find_vectorized(_First_ptr, _STD _To_address(_Last), _Val);
  File "xutility", line 6024, in std::find
    _STD _Seek_wrapped(_First, _STD _Find_unchecked(_STD _Get_unwrapped(_First), _STD _Get_unwrapped(_Last), _Val));
  File "layer.cpp", line 57, in doc::Layer::getPrevious
    std::find(m_parent->layers().begin(),
  File "drop_on_timeline.cpp", line 237, in app::cmd::DropOnTimeline::onUndo
    layerBefore = layer->getPrevious();
  File "cmd.cpp", line 52, in app::Cmd::undo
    onUndo();
...
(20 additional frame(s) were not displayed)
```

Been able to reproduce this as follows:
1. ✨ Create a new file
2. ✨ Drop a png or jpg file at the bottom of the "Layer 1".
3. ✨ Delete the layer that was just created because of the drop.
4. ✨ Undo the deletion.
5. 💥 Try to undo the drop. You can't, it crashes.
